tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM

questions.question: Q: Explain the difference between orthographic and isometric drawings.
questions.correctAnswer: Orthographic shows separate 2D views (front, plan, side) for precise dimensional information. Isometric shows a single 3D view for easier visualisation but less precision for dimensioning.

questions.question: Q: Why is a section view used in engineering drawings?
questions.correctAnswer: A section reveals internal features (holes, chambers, wall thicknesses) hidden in external views. Hatching distinguishes solid material from empty space.

questions.question: Q: Describe the information in an assembly drawing.
questions.correctAnswer: All components in assembled positions with item numbers, a parts list with descriptions, quantities and materials. Overall dimensions but usually not individual part dimensions.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM

questions.question: Q: Explain the CAD/CAM workflow from design to manufactured part.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Create 3D CAD model. 2) Generate 2D drawings with dimensions. 3) Use CAM to create toolpaths. 4) Post-process to G-code. 5) Verify by simulation. 6) Run CNC machine.

questions.question: Q: State three dimensioning rules.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Never duplicate a dimension. 2) Place dimensions between views where possible. 3) Dimension from a common datum for related features.
